questions.text: Portfolio Managers must report performance:
options: Uniformly across disclosure documents, marketing materials, and client reports
questions.explanation: Performance must be disclosed uniformly across all communications, as per SEBI’s performance disclosure norms.

questions.text: Investment, in the context of personal finance, primarily refers to:
options: Holding cash in a locker for emergencies
Committing money to assets expected to generate income or capital growth
Spending on lifestyle items such as vacations and gadgets
Payment of income tax to the government
questions.explanation: Investment involves deploying money into assets with an expectation of future income and/or capital appreciation, not mere spending or idle cash.

questions.text: In personal financial planning, "human capital" refers to:
options: Present value of all future earning capacity of an individual
questions.explanation: Human capital is the economic value of a person’s future earning capacity.

questions.text: Which of the following investors are eligible to invest in AIFs?
options: Resident, NRI and foreign investors, subject to FEMA
questions.explanation: AIFs can accept investment from resident, NRI and foreign investors in compliance with FEMA and SEBI norms.

questions.text: Mark-to-market in futures trading means:
options: Adjusting contract value daily for changes in market price
Fixing profit at the start of the contract
questions.explanation: Mark-to-market involves daily settlement of profit or loss due to price movement, adjusting each participant’s margin account.

questions.text: A positive cash-flow surplus can be used for:
questions.explanation: Surplus cash can build assets or reduce liabilities.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) is TRUE?
options: They require a minimum of ₹10,000 per month
They average out cost by regular periodic investing
They are available only to HNIs
questions.explanation: SIPs invest fixed amounts periodically, enabling rupee cost averaging and disciplined investing.

questions.text: Which of the following is a liquidity constraint?
questions.explanation: Upcoming commitments like tuition or medical expenses create liquidity constraints requiring liquid assets.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: If a complaint remains unresolved even after arbitration, an investor may approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can approach Consumer Courts or High Courts if dissatisfied after arbitration.

questions.text: Before registration, SEBI checks whether the applicant has:
options: At least one branch office in every metro
A qualified Principal Officer and Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: SEBI ensures that the Portfolio Manager has appointed a Principal Officer with relevant qualifications and experience, and a Compliance Officer.

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: Which department of the Ministry of Finance deals with public sector banks, insurance, and pension reforms?
options: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
questions.explanation: The Department of Financial Services administers policies on public sector banks, insurance and pension reforms.

questions.text: Under PMLA, intermediaries must report suspicious transactions to:
questions.explanation: The Financial Intelligence Unit–India (FIU-IND) under the Ministry of Finance receives suspicious transaction reports from intermediaries.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST explains the role of asset allocation?
options: Deciding how to split investments across major asset classes such as equity, debt, and others
Timing entry and exit from a single stock
questions.explanation: Asset allocation determines the proportion of wealth invested in different asset classes and is a key driver of risk and return.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of Modern Portfolio Theory?
options: Investors are rational and risk averse
Investors aim to maximize expected return for a given level of risk
Investors base decisions solely on expected return and risk
Investors prefer portfolios with the highest possible risk
questions.explanation: MPT assumes investors are rational and risk-averse, not risk-seeking; they prefer lower risk for the same level of return.

questions.text: Which factor can negatively affect credit score?
options: High credit-card utilisation and late payments
Mix of secured and unsecured loans
questions.explanation: Late payments and over-utilised credit limits lower scores.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding investor grievance handling?
options: Complaints can only be submitted physically
SCORES allows paperless digital complaint resolution
Investors must pay a fee to file on SCORES
questions.explanation: SCORES provides a free, paperless, and transparent process for investors to submit and monitor complaints online.

questions.text: The Information Ratio evaluates:
options: Excess return relative to benchmark divided by total risk
Excess return relative to benchmark divided by tracking error
Total portfolio return divided by benchmark return
questions.explanation: Information Ratio = (Rp – Rb) / Tracking Error, measuring the manager’s ability to generate active return consistently.

questions.text: Which budgeting method allocates funds first to essential expenses and savings before discretionary spending?
questions.explanation: Pay-yourself-first ensures savings are prioritised before optional spending.

questions.text: Dividends paid on equity shares are:
options: Discretionary and depend on company profits
questions.explanation: Equity dividends are not fixed; the board declares them based on profits and policy.

questions.text: A key first step in the financial planning process is to:
options: Understand the client’s current financial situation and goals
questions.explanation: The planner must first understand the client’s situation, needs and goals before making any recommendations.

questions.text: SEBI’s role in the equity market is to:
options: Regulate issuers and intermediaries, and protect investor interests
Fix the price of every stock
Act as a broker for retail investors
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates markets and intermediaries to ensure fair practices and investor protection.

questions.text: In the context of personal finance, risk tolerance refers to:
options: The ability to pay income tax
The client’s willingness to accept fluctuations in investment value
The number of bank accounts held
questions.explanation: Risk tolerance is about the psychological comfort with volatility and the possibility of loss.

questions.text: Call risk is associated with:
options: Bonds that may be redeemed by the issuer before maturity
Bonds that cannot be sold in the secondary market
Bonds with very long maturities only
questions.explanation: Call risk arises in callable bonds where the issuer may redeem early, forcing the investor to reinvest at possibly lower yields.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, an AMC can offer:
options: Both a value fund and a contra fund
Only a value fund but not a contra fund
Only a contra fund but not a value fund
Either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both
questions.explanation: A mutual fund house can have either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both, as per SEBI categorisation norms.

questions.text: Dividend yield is calculated as:
options: Dividend per share ÷ earnings per share
Dividend per share ÷ market price per share × 100
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = (Dividend per share / Market price) × 100.

questions.text: A zero-based budget approach means:
options: Each rupee of income is assigned to a specific use, leaving zero unallocated
Budget is copied from previous year
questions.explanation: Zero-based budgeting allocates every rupee toward a purpose: spending, saving, or investing.

questions.text: Savings ratio is defined as:
questions.explanation: It measures the proportion of income saved each year.

questions.text: Why is it important to prioritise financial goals?
options: Because only one goal can be achieved
Because resources are usually limited and not all goals can be met simultaneously
To avoid investing in equity products
questions.explanation: Most people face resource constraints, so goals must be ranked to allocate savings effectively.

questions.text: In the grievance process, a complaint is considered 'resolved' when:
options: Investor acknowledges satisfactory resolution or SEBI closes after due examination
questions.explanation: A complaint is treated as resolved when the investor confirms satisfaction or SEBI determines due process is complete.

questions.text: Whose primary responsibility is it to safeguard the interests of investors in a mutual fund?
questions.explanation: Trustees are appointed to oversee the mutual fund and protect the interests of the unit holders.

questions.text: Redemption proceeds of NRI investments made on a non-repatriable basis are credited to:
questions.explanation: Non-repatriable proceeds are credited to the NRO account of the NRI investor.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations correctly matches asset class and its typical characteristic?
options: Government bond – low credit risk, interest rate risk present
Real estate – highly liquid, intraday tradable
questions.explanation: Government bonds usually have low credit risk, but their prices are still affected by changes in interest rates.

questions.text: An Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) is best described as:
options: A retail mutual fund open to all investors
A privately pooled investment vehicle collecting funds from investors for defined investment policy
questions.explanation: AIFs are privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds from investors to invest according to a defined policy for the benefit of investors.

questions.text: EMI stands for:
questions.explanation: EMI is the fixed amount paid by a borrower every month to repay loan principal and interest.

questions.text: Downgrade risk refers to:
options: Risk that rating agencies may upgrade the bond, reducing yield
Risk that the bond’s credit rating is lowered after purchase, causing its market price to fall
Risk that interest rates will fall
Risk that the bond cannot be listed
questions.explanation: If a rating agency downgrades an issuer, investors demand higher yield, causing existing bond prices to fall—this is downgrade risk.

questions.text: A person’s income and expenses both rise 10%. The savings amount:
questions.explanation: If both rise equally in % terms, the rupee surplus remains same proportion.

questions.text: AMFI primarily functions as:
options: A mutual fund industry self-regulatory organization (SRO)
questions.explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is an SRO promoting investor awareness and ethical conduct among mutual funds.

questions.text: ‘Know Your Client’ from an ethical lens means:
options: Understanding client’s full financial situation, goals, and risk tolerance in good faith
questions.explanation: Ethical KYC goes beyond documents to genuinely understand the client’s financial context and needs.

questions.text: A Research Analyst must renew NISM certification every:
questions.explanation: NISM certifications for Research Analysts and Investment Advisers are valid for three years and must be renewed thereafter.

questions.text: If two assets are perfectly positively correlated, diversification will:
options: Have no effect on portfolio risk
questions.explanation: Perfect positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +1) means both assets move identically, offering no diversification benefit.

questions.text: Structured products are best described as:
options: Plain-vanilla equity shares of a company
Pre-packaged investment products combining different instruments to provide a specific payoff profile
questions.explanation: Structured products usually combine underlying assets and derivatives to deliver a targeted payoff, such as capital protection plus limited upside.

questions.text: Category III AIFs are characterised by:
options: Use of diverse or complex trading strategies including leverage
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs, such as hedge funds, employ complex or leverage-based trading strategies and invest in listed or unlisted securities.

questions.text: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: Portfolio Management Services are governed by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the earlier 1993 regulations.

questions.text: The interest component of an EMI in the first few months is:
questions.explanation: Initially, outstanding principal is high; hence interest dominates early EMIs.

questions.text: The overarching ethical test for any adviser action is:
options: Will it pass regulatory scrutiny alone?
Is it legal, fair, transparent, and in the client’s best interest?
questions.explanation: Ethical actions must be legal, fair, transparent, and aligned with the client’s best interests and market integrity.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio measures:
options: Loan amount ÷ Value of underlying asset
questions.explanation: LTV shows how much of the asset’s value is financed through borrowing.

questions.text: The process of finding the present value from a known future value is called:
questions.explanation: Discounting is the reverse of compounding.

questions.text: Which statement about emergency funds is MOST appropriate in the context of financial planning?
options: They are optional for salaried individuals
They should ideally cover 3 to 6 months of essential expenses
They should always be invested in equity funds
They are required only close to retirement
questions.explanation: A commonly used rule of thumb is to maintain 3–6 months of essential expenses in liquid form as an emergency fund.

questions.text: Which of the following occurs in the primary market?
options: Issue of new securities by companies to investors
Purchase of shares on the stock exchange
Sale of government securities by RBI in the secondary market
questions.explanation: The primary market facilitates the issue of new securities by companies to raise funds from investors.

questions.text: Portfolio risk depends on:
options: Variances and covariances between all assets in the portfolio
questions.explanation: Portfolio risk depends not just on the variance of each asset but also on their covariance or correlation.

questions.text: The key compliance requirement for all intermediaries under SEBI is:
options: Filing annual audit reports with SEBI
Maintaining client confidentiality and proper records
questions.explanation: Intermediaries must maintain confidentiality and records as part of SEBI’s code of conduct and inspection norms.

questions.text: In the BB&K model, 'Guardians' are investors who:
options: Focus on wealth preservation and avoid volatility
questions.explanation: Guardians are cautious investors focused on preserving wealth and avoiding high volatility, often seen near retirement age.

questions.text: A Government Security (G-Sec) is best described as:
options: An unsecured equity instrument issued by RBI
A tradable debt instrument issued by Central or State Government
questions.explanation: G-Secs are tradable debt instruments issued by the Central or State Governments acknowledging the government’s debt obligation.

questions.text: Large-cap funds, as defined by SEBI, must invest at least:
options: 50% of total assets in large-cap stocks
65% of total assets in large-cap stocks
80% of total assets in large-cap stocks
100% of total assets in large-cap stocks
questions.explanation: To qualify as a large-cap fund, at least 80% of total assets must be invested in large-cap companies (ranks 1–100 by full market cap as per AMFI list).

questions.text: IRDAI is the regulator for:
questions.explanation: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates the insurance sector.

questions.text: The secondary market provides:
options: Liquidity and continuous price discovery for existing securities
questions.explanation: The secondary market offers liquidity and price discovery by allowing investors to trade existing securities.

questions.text: Rebalancing of a portfolio is required primarily because:
options: Asset prices change over time altering allocation weights
questions.explanation: Rebalancing restores the portfolio’s asset allocation to its target mix after market movements cause deviations.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly represents discounting at rate r for n years?
questions.explanation: Discounting divides by (1 + r)ⁿ.

questions.text: Minimum net worth required for registration of a Portfolio Manager under SEBI (2020) Regulations is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: The price paid by an option buyer to the seller is called:
questions.explanation: The option premium is paid upfront by the buyer to the seller for acquiring the right embedded in the option.

questions.text: If an investor remains unsatisfied after SCORES closure, the next escalation is to:
options: Ombudsman or Arbitration mechanism at exchange or SEBI-recognized body
questions.explanation: Investors may approach SEBI’s Ombudsman or exchange arbitration for unresolved cases.

questions.text: Angel Funds are a sub-category of:
questions.explanation: Angel Funds are registered under Category I AIFs and invest in early-stage start-ups meeting specific criteria.

questions.text: Correlation coefficient ranges between:
questions.explanation: Correlation values range between -1 and +1, where -1 indicates perfect negative and +1 perfect positive correlation.

questions.text: Which of these improves the current ratio (liquid assets ÷ current liabilities)?
questions.explanation: Reducing liabilities with existing cash improves ratio.

questions.text: Rights issues allow existing shareholders to:
options: Buy additional shares at a discount in proportion to holdings
Sell their shares to promoters only
questions.explanation: Rights issues give existing shareholders preferential rights to buy new shares, usually at a discount.

questions.text: Primary market refers to:
options: Trading of existing securities among investors
Issue of new securities by issuers to investors
Trading of commodities like gold and oil
questions.explanation: In the primary market, issuers raise fresh capital by issuing securities to investors for the first time.

questions.text: Net Asset Value (NAV) per unit is calculated as:
options: Net assets divided by face value
Number of units divided by net assets
Net assets divided by number of outstanding units
Total investments divided by number of investors
questions.explanation: NAV per unit = Net assets / Number of outstanding units.

questions.text: Which is an example of DIRECT investment by a retail investor?
options: Buying a diversified equity mutual fund
Investing through a PMS in multiple stocks
Buying listed shares of a company in her own demat account
Investing in a Category II AIF
questions.explanation: Buying shares directly in a demat account is a direct investment; mutual funds, PMS and AIFs are managed/pooled vehicles.

questions.text: Which of these is the least expensive form of credit?
questions.explanation: Gold loan is secured and typically has lower interest than unsecured credit.

questions.text: The Rule of 72 gives:
options: Exact number of years to double an amount
Approximate years to double money at given rate
Half of the rate of return
questions.explanation: Rule of 72 approximates doubling time = 72 ÷ rate of return.

questions.text: Over-leveraging occurs when:
options: Liabilities are disproportionately high compared to income or assets
questions.explanation: Excessive borrowing relative to capacity leads to financial strain.

questions.text: In the context of mutual fund transactions, RTA stands for:
questions.explanation: RTA stands for Registrar and Transfer Agent, entities that handle investor servicing and record maintenance for AMCs.

questions.text: Equity as an asset class represents:
options: A fixed claim on company’s assets and income
An ownership stake in a company
A loan given to the government
A derivative contract based on commodities
questions.explanation: Equity represents ownership in a company, with residual claim on assets and income after obligations to lenders are met.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a financial investment asset?
options: Gold jewellery used for personal wear
Equity shares of a listed company
questions.explanation: Equity shares are a financial investment asset. Gold jewellery and personal-use assets are primarily consumption assets, not pure financial investments.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: Money market instruments generally include all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Money market instruments have maturities below one year; 10-year bonds are capital market instruments.

questions.text: For arbitration of disputes between investors and brokers, the forum used is:
questions.explanation: Exchange arbitration panels handle disputes between investors and brokers as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

questions.text: Inspection of intermediaries by SEBI is conducted to:
options: Ensure compliance with laws and regulations
questions.explanation: SEBI inspects intermediaries to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and investor protection norms.

questions.text: A 'risk-seeking' investor is one who:
options: Engages willingly in fair games with uncertain outcomes
questions.explanation: Risk-seeking investors make an upward adjustment to utility for risk, willingly engaging in fair games.

questions.text: A key distinguishing feature of a mutual fund compared to PMS is that:
options: Mutual funds are unregulated, while PMS is regulated
Mutual funds pool money from many investors into a common portfolio, while PMS maintains segregated portfolios for each client
Mutual funds are only for HNIs, while PMS is for small investors
Mutual funds can invest only in equity
questions.explanation: Mutual funds operate a common pool of assets, whereas PMS typically runs segregated portfolios in each client’s name.

questions.text: The main cost associated with frequent rebalancing is:
questions.explanation: Rebalancing involves brokerage and tax implications from buying and selling securities.

questions.text: Which of the following is a non-recurring expense?
questions.explanation: Vacations occur occasionally and are non-recurring.

questions.text: An unsecured loan is one that:
options: Has no underlying asset pledged to the lender
questions.explanation: Unsecured loans rely solely on borrower’s creditworthiness rather than collateral.

questions.text: An IPO is:
options: A loan from public to the company
The first public sale of shares by a company
A share buyback by the company
questions.explanation: Initial Public Offer is the first time a company offers shares to the public to raise equity capital.

questions.text: The SCORES platform was launched by SEBI in:
questions.explanation: SEBI launched the SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redress System) in 2011 to digitize grievance handling.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of an Investment Policy Statement?
options: To help set realistic return expectations
To provide framework for evaluating the portfolio manager
To protect investors from unethical behaviour
questions.explanation: The IPS provides structure and accountability but does not guarantee investment returns.

questions.text: AIFs must issue to investors:
options: A Key Information Memorandum similar to mutual funds
questions.explanation: AIFs raise funds through private placement by issuing a detailed Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) to investors.

questions.case_text: Ajay, aged 42, plans to retire at 60. His monthly expenses are ₹80,000, expected to rise by 5% annually. He expects 8% post-retirement returns and wants his corpus to last till age 85.

questions.text: Years left for retirement:

questions.text: Rakesh’s risk profile is:
Short-term goal is:
Approximate investment horizon for retirement goal:

questions.case_text: Neha received ₹5 lakh bonus and is considering investing either lump sum in an equity fund or via SIP over 12 months. The fund’s long-term return expectation is 10% per annum, and markets are volatile.

questions.text: Bonus amount received:

questions.case_text: Nisha has three loans — car loan ₹5 lakh at 11%, personal loan ₹3 lakh at 13%, and credit card outstanding ₹1 lakh at 36%. She considers consolidating them into a single loan at 12% for 4 years.

questions.text: Which loan has the highest rate?
Total current outstanding debt:
Proposed consolidated loan rate:
Main advantage of consolidation:
Highest priority loan to prepay is:

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:
If Rohit takes a loan, tenure is:
Investment return from the mutual fund is:
Which option gives higher effective return?
What factor mainly decides his choice?
options: Difference between loan rate and investment return

questions.case_text: Priya and Kunal are a salaried couple earning ₹9 lakh and ₹12 lakh per year respectively. They invest in ELSS and PPF and pay a home loan interest of ₹2.5 lakh annually. They want to optimise Section 80C and 24(b) benefits.
